items.followUp: Define rest and motion, giving one example of each.

rubric.why: Rest is defined relative to the surroundings.
rubric.description: Defines rest relative to the surroundings.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that an object's position does not change with time relative to its surroundings.

rubric.why: Motion is defined relative to the surroundings.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining motion as a change in position with time relative to the surroundings, with suitable examples of rest and motion.

modelAnswer: An object is at rest if its position does not change with time relative to its surroundings.
An object is in motion if its position changes with time relative to its surroundings.
A book lying on a table is at rest; a moving car is in motion.

rubric.why: Dynamics concerns motion together with its causes.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for stating that dynamics is the branch of mechanics that studies motion and the forces causing it; award 1 mark if only motion or only the role of forces is correctly mentioned.

modelAnswer: Dynamics is the branch of mechanics that studies the motion of bodies and the forces that cause this motion.

items.followUp: Define the pivot and moment arm for a force acting on a lever.

rubric.why: The line of action describes the direction along which the force acts.
rubric.description: Defines the line of action of a force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as the imaginary straight line along which the force acts.

rubric.why: The moment arm is measured perpendicularly from the pivot or axis to the line of action.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it is the perpendicular distance from the pivot or axis of rotation to the line of action.

modelAnswer: The line of action of a force is the imaginary straight line along which the force acts.
The moment arm is the perpendicular distance from the pivot or axis of rotation to the line of action of the force.

items.followUp: Write the formula for the moment of a force and state whether it is a vector or scalar quantity.

rubric.why: The moment is calculated from force and its perpendicular distance from the pivot.
rubric.description: Gives the formula for moment of force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for moment = force × perpendicular distance from the pivot or axis.

rubric.why: The moment of force has both magnitude and direction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as a vector quantity.

modelAnswer: Moment of force = force × perpendicular distance from the pivot to the line of action of the force.
The moment of force is a vector quantity.

items.followUp: Define one joule of work and state its SI unit.

rubric.why: The SI unit of power is the watt.
rubric.description: Names the SI unit of power.

rubric.why: Power is the rate of doing work or transferring energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that one watt is the power when one joule of work is done in one second.

modelAnswer: The SI unit of power is the watt (W).
One watt is the power when one joule of work is done in one second.

items.followUp: What is energy? State one use of energy in daily life.

rubric.why: Energy is required to do work.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that energy is needed to do work.

rubric.why: A suitable example demonstrates a use of energy.
rubric.description: Gives an example of a use of energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid example, such as running machines, moving objects, cooking, lighting or heating.

modelAnswer: We need energy to do work.
For example, energy is needed to move objects and to run machines.

items.followUp: What is a thermometer? Give one reason alcohol or mercury is used in it.

rubric.why: A thermometer is an instrument for measuring temperature.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it is an instrument used to measure temperature.

rubric.why: A suitable property explains why mercury is useful as a thermometric substance.
rubric.description: Gives a reason mercury is preferred.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one correct reason, such as its uniform expansion, visibility, not wetting glass, or ability to measure a wide range of temperatures.

modelAnswer: A thermometer is an instrument used to measure temperature.
Mercury is preferred as a thermometric substance because it expands uniformly and does not wet the glass; it is also easily visible.

items.followUp: State Newton's First Law of Motion and explain what is meant by inertia.

rubric.why: Newton's Second Law relates force to the rate of change of momentum.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the rate of change of momentum is proportional to the applied force and occurs in the force's direction.

rubric.why: The proportionality between force and the rate of change of momentum is the starting point of the derivation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for writing force proportional to change in momentum divided by time.

rubric.why: Substituting momentum and acceleration connects the law to mass and acceleration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for using p = mv and a = (v − u)/t to obtain the relation in terms of mass and acceleration.

rubric.why: F = ma is the resulting equation of Newton's Second Law in SI units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for deriving or stating F = ma.

modelAnswer: Newton's Second Law: The rate of change of momentum of a body is directly proportional to the applied force and takes place in the direction of that force.
Force is proportional to the rate of change of momentum: F ∝ (final momentum − initial momentum)/time.
For a body of constant mass m changing velocity from u to v in time t, change in momentum = mv − mu = m(v − u).
Acceleration a = (v − u)/t, so F ∝ m(v − u)/t = ma.
In SI units the proportionality constant is 1; therefore, F = ma.
